clue.text: Rival to Valentine's Day shortened by Zeus's lover

indicators.note: shortened tells us the day named is cut down, keeping only its opening stretch

parts.note: the day here is Thursday, of which only the start is kept
Io was a mortal loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A rival to St Valentine's Day, made shorter by a lover of the king of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Valentine's Day' reads as one phrase, but Valentine belongs to the definition (Valentine of The Two Gentlemen of Verona) and Day starts the wordplay; 'shortened' cuts THURSDAY to THUR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona, the foolish suitor Thurio competes with Valentine for Silvia's hand.

clue.text: He is an awkward stranger Bruno meets on a train

definitions.text: stranger Bruno meets on a train

indicators.note: awkward suggests the three words are clumsily arranged and must be put in another order

explanation.surface: An awkward stranger is the man Bruno encounters on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' looks like a description of the stranger but signals an anagram of HE IS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Highsmith's novel Strangers on a Train, the tennis player Guy Haines is the passenger Bruno Anthony meets and draws into a murder pact.

clue.text: Paper, possibly "Black and White"

definitions.meaning: a tabloid newspaper is disparagingly called by this name
the Black and White ... is a ragtime piano tune by George Botsford

explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a newspaper's name, which matches the first sense, but it is a piece of ragtime, famous in Britain as the theme of the snooker show Pot Black.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper, and the piece called Black and White is a rag in the ragtime sense.

clue.text: About 25, he briefly loses Faith in Hope Leslie

definitions.text: he briefly loses Faith in Hope Leslie

parts.note: about means on, as in a talk on a subject
the answer to 25 down is the novelist Umberto Eco

explanation.surface: Around a quarter-century, a man loses his faith, so the story runs, in a novel of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' is a cross-reference to 25 down, not a number. Faith Leslie, sister of the heroine of Sedgwick's novel Hope Leslie, marries the Pequot Oneco and is lost to her family.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneco is the Native American character in Catharine Sedgwick's 1827 novel Hope Leslie who marries Faith Leslie and takes her away from the settlers.

clue.text: A Robert Antoni novel: one with very erotic covers

indicators.note: covers says the sexy word wraps around the other two pieces

parts.note: erotic means carnal, of the flesh
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A novel by Robert Antoni: a book with racy jacket designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' sounds like book jackets but tells you CARNAL goes round IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnival (2005) is a novel by the Trinidadian-American writer Robert Antoni set around Trinidad's festival season.

clue.text: Merchant who offers his wife Celia my Chianti?

definitions.text: Merchant who offers his wife Celia

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
Chianti is a wine, Italian vino

explanation.surface: A trader offers his wife to a guest along with a glass of his Tuscan red.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is everyday British slang for surprise, just as 'my!' is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jonson's Volpone the jealous merchant Corvino offers his wife Celia to Volpone in hope of an inheritance.

clue.text: O to be recruited by music's top firm!

indicators.note: to be recruited by means to join the ranks of, so the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: rock is a kind of music; with its 's this gives ROCKS
a top or cover is a lid

explanation.surface: An exclamation of longing to be signed by the music industry's leading label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O to be' reads like a poetic sigh, as in Browning's 'Oh, to be in England', but the O is a letter that 'to be recruited by' drops into the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely solid and dependable is called unshakeable or firm.

clue.text: Novel written by popular journalist put together with twists

parts.note: in means popular, as in the in thing

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters of the next word are made into something new

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A book penned by a well-known reporter, assembled with plenty of plot turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal, rearranging 'written' between the two short pieces; 'by' just places them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads that are twisted round one another are braided or wound together.

clue.text: River in a European capital is the setting for Cold Granite

indicators.note: in places the river inside the capital's name

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales

explanation.surface: A river running through a continental capital is the scene of a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee really does flow through Aberdeen, which makes the surface sound factual.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuart MacBride's crime novel Cold Granite is set in the Scottish city known as the Granite City.

clue.text: Play card and pick up the last discarded

parts.note: a king is a court card

indicators.note: the last discarded drops the final letter of the verb for picking up

parts.note: to pick up a skill is to learn it

explanation.surface: Lay down a card and then draw the most recently thrown-away one from the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a card-game instruction; 'Play' is the definition, and 'discarded' is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy of an old king and his three daughters.

clue.text: She wrote of the Great Plains Lion, perhaps before this woman

definitions.text: She wrote of the Great Plains

indicators.note: before places the animal ahead of the pronoun

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
this woman, as the object of a sentence, is her

explanation.surface: A writer about the prairies, perhaps with a lion ahead of her.
explanation.definitionFit: Willa Cather's novels such as My Ántonia and O Pioneers! portray settlers on the Nebraska prairie.

clue.text: Timon's friend's sermon is up for review

indicators.note: for review suggests the letters are to be gone over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend of Timon's has his sermon put up to be criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'up for review' but is the end of the anagram fodder SERMON IS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sempronius is one of the false friends in Shakespeare's Timon of Athens who refuse Timon money.

clue.text: Slender servant's spot full of misshapen trees

indicators.note: full of says the spot holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a spot on the skin is a pimple

indicators.note: misshapen says the letters of the following word are bent into a new form

explanation.surface: The servant's patch is crowded with crooked trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slender' looks like an adjective but is Master Slender of The Merry Wives of Windsor; 'misshapen' rearranges 'trees', and 'full of' sets the result inside the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merry Wives of Windsor, Peter Simple is the manservant of the foolish suitor Abraham Slender.

clue.text: Outspoken, clear foe of the Doones

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out loud, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to clear is to rid

explanation.surface: A frank, plain-speaking enemy of the outlaw Doone family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken, clear' looks like a description of a person, but it signals a word that is pronounced like RID.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ridd, hero of Blackmore's Lorna Doone, fights the outlaw Doone clan of Exmoor.

clue.text: A poem meaningless in subject and name 6,

indicators.note: in puts the empty word inside the topic

parts.note: a subject or topic is a theme
hollow words are empty, meaningless

explanation.surface: A poem empty of meaning in its theme and its title.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held ends in a stray '6,', a fragment of the enumeration (3,6,3); it has no job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollow Men is a 1925 poem by T. S. Eliot ending 'Not with a bang but a whimper'.

clue.text: Book Dromio and Antipholus, not the Syracusans

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament, Paul's letter to the church at Ephesus

definitions.text: Dromio and Antipholus, not the Syracusans
definitions.meaning: in The Comedy of Errors each pair of twins has one brother from Ephesus and one from Syracuse

explanation.walkthrough: Both Dromio and Antipholus come in twin pairs; ruling out the Syracusan pair leaves the brothers from Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Ephesus are so called, and Paul's letter to that city's church is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Anglican, say, but not an English novelist

indicators.note: not says the little word is taken away from the believer

parts.note: an Anglican is an example of a Christian
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Anglican, perhaps, though not an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not an English novelist' reads as one phrase, but 'not an' removes AN from CHRISTIAN and English then adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote the Poirot and Miss Marple detective novels.

clue.text: Clay pipe maybe Septimus Harding laid next to St. Cuthbert's?

indicators.note: laid next to sets the two pieces side by side

parts.note: St Cuthbert's is a church, the Barchester parish Harding later holds
Septimus Harding is the title character of Trollope's novel The Warden

explanation.surface: A long clay pipe, perhaps, set down by Trollope's clergyman beside his parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe; Harding, warden of Hiram's Hospital in The Warden, later becomes rector of St Cuthbert's.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe takes its name from the lay church officers said to have smoked it.

clue.text: One Steele initially brought in to supplement

definitions.text: One Steele initially brought in to supplement

indicators.note: brought in to says the two letters are placed inside the extra piece

parts.note: to supplement is to add on
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the essayist's surname

explanation.surface: A man whom Steele first brought in to boost his paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Joseph Addison joined Richard Steele's Tatler and became his partner on The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison, the essayist, was Steele's collaborator on The Tatler and The Spectator.

clue.text: Do something brilliant in Colchis

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle them
Jason sailed to Colchis to win the Golden ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do something brilliant' reads as one phrase meaning excel, but 'Do' is a definition alone, slang for cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To con or overcharge someone is to swindle, and the golden pelt of the ram was kept at Colchis.

clue.text: Musical concert opening in Idaho

parts.note: a gig is a concert

indicators.note: opening in takes the first letter of the state's name

explanation.surface: A show's opening concert held in Idaho.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical, filmed in 1958.

clue.text: How some trot out pages to confuse

parts.note: pages of writing are sides
to confuse is to addle

explanation.surface: Some people produce pages simply to muddle the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trot out' looks like 'produce', but here it means ride out at a trot.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding with both legs on one side of the horse is how women once rode out.

clue.text: To be Lady Crawley, Becky is keen

definitions.meaning: Becky's maiden surname before she married Rawdon Crawley in Vanity Fair
keen as in having a fine edge

explanation.walkthrough: Becky Sharp of Thackeray's Vanity Fair becomes Lady Crawley when her husband Rawdon inherits the baronetcy.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade is a sharp one, and Becky's maiden name in Vanity Fair is the same word.

clue.text: More work and nowhere to translate it

definitions.meaning: a book by Sir Thomas More, the work of More
the Greek coinage means no place

explanation.walkthrough: 'More work' looks like 'extra labour', but More is Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary island republic is named from Greek ou (not) and topos (place).

clue.text: Part including a few incomplete verses by Masefield

indicators.note: including means the cutting word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to part is to sever

indicators.note: incomplete drops the final letter of the small quantity word

explanation.surface: A section containing a handful of unfinished lines by the poet Masefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a noun but is the verb sever, holding A and FE (FEW cut short).
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-Fever, beginning 'I must go down to the seas again', is John Masefield's best-known poem.

clue.text: Finally, the epic Numero Zero author

definitions.text: Finally, the epic Numero Zero author

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: At last, the grand writer of the novel Numero Zero.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the author of Numero Zero is Umberto Eco, and the end letters of 'the epic Numero' spell his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist, published Numero Zero in 2015.

clue.text: Being entertaining and French gets you a Musical Oscar

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the French word is put inside

parts.note: a being is a person
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Being entertaining and French earns you an Academy Award for a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical Oscar' looks like an Academy Award but is Oscar Peterson, the jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist, a musician of world renown.

clue.text: Poet or enigmatic diarist?

indicators.note: enigmatic hints at a puzzle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Is this a poet, or a mysterious keeper of a journal?
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Pooter is the fictional author of The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith.
